item.title: Public health specialist discusses the aftermath of the munitions detonation in Iowa
item.description: NPR's A Martinez speaks with public health specialist Will Sander of the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign about the aftermath of the Iowa munitions detonation.
item.dc:creator: A Martínez

item.title: How American Thanksgiving took root -- and evolved -- in Liberia
item.description: The first settlers of Liberia were African Americans who brought along the holiday of Thanksgiving — which has evolved to reflect the history and identity of this new nation.
item.dc:creator: Ari Daniel

item.title: This group of seamstresses mends shirts to make chemo easier for cancer patients
item.description: Seamstresses in Ohio and other states are making zippered shirts for cancer patients so they can more comfortably undergo chemotherapy treatments.
item.dc:creator: Kendall Crawford

item.title: Here's the public health guidance for possible lead exposure in Iowa
item.description: NPR's Juana Summers talks with Dr. Dan McCabe, medical director of the Iowa Poison Control Center, about how people can protect themselves after the Army detonates degraded lead azide.
item.dc:creator: Michelle Aslam

item.title: Doctors struggle to save babies after parents refuse vitamin K
item.description: Doctors are fighting an uphill battle against disinformation about routine vitamin K shots given to newborns in the hospital. It helps prevent a rare but devastating bleeding disorder.
item.dc:creator: Kate Wells
